jobs.occupation: PhD Student in Acute Leukemia Research - Department of Hematology / Oncology (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: ...you're in the middle of itThe Department of Hematology/Oncology  of the university hospital in Frankfurt offers a broad diagnostic and therapeutic spectrum for patients with solid tumors, as well as malignant diseases of the hematopoietic system and investigates its development, progression, as well as therapy resistance. The Max-Eder Junior Research Group (funded by the German Cancer Aid) lead by Dr. med. Anjali Cremer is dedicated to deciphering oncogenic signaling transduction mechanisms, identification and characterization of viability regulators, as well as the analyses of resistance mechanisms to targeted therapies in acute leukemia.Dr. med. Anjali Cremer's team investigate new therapeutic vulnerabilities, that overcome resistance mechanisms in acute leukemia. The lab itself is embedded in the excellent re-search infrastructure of the university hospital in Frankfurt. Leukemia research and re-search on clonal hematopoiesis is one of the main focusses of the Department of Hematology/Oncology, as well as of the Frankfurt Cancer Institute and the DKTK partner site Frankfurt. Moreover, there are multiple possibilities for collaborations with scientists from all over the world.The position is fixed-term for a period of three years .Your Role :- The project is based on a recently published study by Bröchtel et al., in which USP22 was identified as key regulator of MEIS1 expression in KMT2A-rearranged acute leukemia. Results were published in the top hematology journal Blood (https://doi.org/10.1182/blood.2025031845).- The PhD project aims to further dissect the interplay between epigenetic regulation and the ubiquitin-proteasome system in order to identify new potential therapeutic interventions.- Your tasks include the design of scientific projects as well as planning, establishing and critically analyzing in vitro as well as in vivo experiments.- To answer our scientific questions, we apply the following experimental techniques (among others): innovative CRISPR-Cas9 knockout and screening technologies, quantitative global, phospho and ubiquitin proteomics, RNAseq, CUT&Tag/ChIP-based chromatin profiling, next-generation DNA Sequencing, FACS analysis and cell sorting, analysis of proteasomal degradation, work with primary patient samples, access to clinical patient data, and in vivo mouse models (C57BL/6 or NSG mice).... your skills are what we're looking for- The applicant should hold a master degree or equivalent in biology, biochemistry, molecular medicine or related fields.- A high level of motivation, flexibility and responsibility as well as very good communication skills in German or English are expected.- Expertise in experimental techniques (e.g. genome editing; high throughput sequencing analyses, flow cytometry) is an advantage.- Experience in animal experiments (FELASA B or C certificate) is an advantage.- Motivation to learn, apply and establish new techniques, ability to critically analyze and reflect data.- Experience with bioinformatic analyses (e.g. RNAseq, NGS) is an advantage.- Good skills with the following programs GraphPad Prism, FlowJo, Adobe Illustrator is an advantage.- Good English language skills.- Due to legal requirements, valid proof of measles immunity or measles vaccination is required.... you'll be offered a lot- In addition to an attractive salary based on acollective agreement (TV-G-U)with an annual special payment, you benefit from long-term security through company pension schemes- Internal and external training for your professional development- Benefit from our attractive health offers. jobs.occupation: Postdoc Researcher (f/m/d) in Evolutionary Genomics of Mammals (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN) , headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre (SBiK-F), starting as soon as possible :Postdoc Researcher (m/f/d)in Evolutionary Genomics of Mammals(Full time / part time ** ** options available)﻿Location: Frankfurt am MainEmployment scope: Full-time; part time options are availableType of contract: Temporary, limited to 2 yearsRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The mission of the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre is to study the complex interactions between biodiversity and climate change.There is an exciting opportunity for a talented and motivated applicant to join the working group of Prof. Dr. Axel Janke. The applicant will be closely involved in gene flow, evolutionary, population or phylo-genetics to study speciation in mammals (bears, giraffe, kangaroos or allies) at the genomic level and in MSc and BSc teaching. Strong own and proven research interests including other vertebrate groups will be considered.Your tasks- Conduct genomic research on mammalian evolution and speciation, including evolutionary, population and phylogenomic analyses- Investigate phylogenetic relationships, gene flow and genomic signatures (possibly QTL and GWAS, genetic load) of evolutionary and environmental processes using genomic and bioinformatic approaches- Apply and further develop bioinformatic methods for the analysis of genomic data, including population genomics, genome assembly and species distribution modelling- Organise and teach university courses and supervise BSc and MSc theses- Independently prepare and publish research results in peer-reviewed journals and contribute to the acquisition of third-party fundingYour profile- PhD degree in Biology, Genetics, Bioinformatics or a related field- Strong interest and proven skills in evolutionary, population or phylogenomics.- Knowledge of gene-flow analyses and/or drift processes is an advantage- Experience in population genomics, genome assembly and script programming, including R- Very good written and oral communication skills in English- Interest in species distribution modelling, paternal inference, conservation genetics and epigeneticsWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, gender, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or disability. Women are particularly encouraged to apply, as they are underrepresented in the field of this position; in the case of equal qualifications and suitability they will be given preference. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application as a single PDF by 10 December2026 , including:- CV- Letter of motivation- Academic transcripts and certificates/credentials- Two relevant publications- Contact details of two potential referencesPlease compress the files where possible. If the two publications cause the file to exceed the upload limit, they may be uploaded separately.Please submit your application via our online application system. If you are viewing this vacancy on an external job platform, please visit our careers page and apply via the corresponding "Apply" button. Applications submitted by email cannot be considered.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt am MainFor specific questions about this role, please contact Prof. Dr. Axel Janke ataxel.janke@senckenberg.deFor data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/Please visit our website at www.senckenberg.de for further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung.

jobs.occupation: Laser Engineer / Optical Engineer (m/f/d) (Ingenieur/in - Augenoptik, Optometrie)
jobs.description: The Max Planck Society is Germany's premier research organization. The 85 Max Planck Institutes conduct research at highest levels, in the service of the general public, in the natural sciences, life sciences, social sciences, and the humanities.At the Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter (MPSD), around 180 staff members and guests investigate how the structure of solids determines their dynamic properties. The institute is located on the Bahrenfeld research campus in Hamburg, in the immediate vicinity of DESY and the University of Hamburg.Ultrashort pulses of light can be used to deliberately change the properties of quantum materials. For picoseconds and longer, a solid can become superconducting or its magnetic and crystal structure can rearrange. This fundamental research is made possible by highly advanced laser systems and complex optical setups. To operate and further develop them, we are looking for aLaser Engineer / Optical Engineer (m/f/d)In the laser laboratories of the Quantum Condensed Matter Dynamics department, we study how the electronic, magnetic and structural properties of quantum materials can be controlled with light. For our time-resolved optical experiments, we operate femtosecond laser systems and nonlinear optical sources that cover a broad spectral range from the visible to the terahertz regime. In addition, we carry out time-resolved X-ray experiments at free-electron lasers worldwide. Further details can be found on our website https://qcmd.mpsd.mpg.de (https://qcmd.mpsd.mpg.de/) .Your responsibilitiesYou ensure that our femtosecond laser systems and optical setups run reliably and continue to evolve, working closely with our team of scientists.In detail, your tasks include:- Operation and regular alignment of our femtosecond amplifiers and nonlinear optical sources (e.g. OPAs, difference frequency conversion, THz generation)- Planning and building new optical setups, from beam delivery to commissioning- CAD design of opto-mechanical components and vacuum parts, and coordination with our mechanical workshop from drawing to installation- Regular maintenance of the laser systems and their peripherals (cooling, vacuum pumps), and coordination of service and repairs with external companies- Support during beamtimes at free-electron lasers as neededYour profileYou have- A Master’s degree in optics, photonics, laser technology, engineering physics or a related field- Alternatively, a Bachelor’s degree with relevant professional experience- Hands-on experience with ultrafast lasers and with building and aligning optical systems- Knowledge of nonlinear optics and optical measurement techniques- Proficiency in CAD software (preferably Autodesk Inventor)- Experience with vacuum technology and optical simulation (e.g. Zemax)- A careful, independent working style and enjoyment of working in an international team- Very good command of English and GermanWhat we offerThe position is initially limited to 2 years, with the possibility of conversion to a permanent contract. Salary and social benefits are based on qualifications and in accordance with the collective agreement for the German public sector (TVöD).Are you insterested?Please apply exclusively via our online application portal.The Max Planck Society seeks to employ more individuals with severe disabilities. Applications from individuals with severe disabilities are expressly encouraged.The Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. We welcome applications from all backgrounds.For further information, please contact Dr. Michael Först (phone +49 40 8998-88105, email: michael.foerst@mpsd.mpg.de (https://www.b-ite.com/recruitingmanager/api/v3/job-postings/c5aebe39-8931-4b83-9f2f-9d396b13d2f9/michael.foerst@mpsd.mpg.de) ) or Dr. Michele Buzzi (phone +49 40 8998-88115, email: michele.buzzi@mpsd.mpg.de (https://mailto:michele.buzzi@mpsd.mpg.de) ).More information is available on our website: http://www.mpsd.mpg.de/karriere/jobs.We look forward to receiving your complete application in English by 15 December 2026
